How can an acid-equivalent concentration fall while the annual acid load stays unchanged?

Use after the [deposition exercises](../deposition/exercise.qmd), alongside [environmental amounts](../environmental-systems/notes.qmd).

## Predict first

If annual water export doubles at the same acid flux and catchment area, predict which quantities change: flux, annual load, or flow-weighted equivalent concentration.

## Questions to try

1. Choose **Worked example**. Calculate the two acid contributions by hand. HNO₃ supplies one equivalent per mole; H₂SO₄ supplies two for the stated full-neutralisation convention.
2. Choose **Double water export**. Explain why annual load is unchanged while equivalent concentration halves.
3. Return to the worked example, then choose **Double catchment area**. The water export is held fixed only for this sensitivity exercise. Explain why this increases load and equivalent concentration.
4. Set both acid inputs to zero. Verify that increasing water volume cannot create an acid input.

## Hand check and static reference

| Quantity | Worked example | Double water export |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HNO₃ contribution | 20000 eq/year | 20000 eq/year |
| H₂SO₄ contribution | 20000 eq/year | 20000 eq/year |
| Total acid load | 40000 eq/year | 40000 eq/year |
| Before-neutralisation equivalent concentration | 0.0800 meq/L | 0.0400 meq/L |

The input fluxes are 20.0 mmol HNO₃ and 10.0 mmol H₂SO₄ per m² per year.
Area is 1.00 km² = 10⁶ m². Annual water export is initially 500 million L.
The equivalent flux is `(20 + 2 × 10)/1000 = 0.0400 eq/m²/year`.
Multiply by area, divide by annual export, then multiply eq/L by 1000 to obtain meq/L.

## Model conditions

The fluxes are **supplied acid inputs**, not sulfate or nitrate measurements assumed to be free acid. All stipulated input is assumed to be routed into the annual exported water, with no storage, other retention, or acid-equivalent sinks. This is the boundary condition that lets input load divided by annual water export represent a hypothetical outlet-equivalent concentration. Catchment neutralisation is excluded here; the [week 5 budget](week5.qmd) introduces it. These are annual flow-weighted quantities. They neither predict pH nor describe a sudden closed-lake acid pulse. Area and water export are independent controls in this deliberately isolated sensitivity model.

## Explain the result

Why is the week 1 value 0.0800 meq/L different from the residual acidity in the integrated catchment example? Identify the process omitted here.
